text: A mapping data flow is Data Factory's visual, code-free transformation tool — exactly the ELT-style transformation step that follows a Copy activity landing raw data. You design the transformation logic visually, and Data Factory translates it into real Spark code, optimizes it, and runs it on a managed, scaled-out cluster you never have to provision or maintain yourself.
Creating one starts the exact same way as everything else in this course. From Factory Resources, select the plus icon, then Data Flow — and you land directly on the authoring canvas, ready to build.

Every data flow opens onto the same three-part surface. The top bar holds validation and the debug toggle Lesson 24 covers next. The graph shows the actual transformation stream itself — source, through however many transformations, into one or more sinks. And the configuration panel shows settings for whatever's currently selected.

Every single transformation carries an Inspect tab, showing the real shape of the data flowing through it — column count, names, types, exactly what changed at this specific step. This is genuinely read-only metadata — you don't need debug mode turned on at all to see it, unlike Lesson 24's Data Preview.

Design it visually, Data Factory translates it into Spark code automatically, and it runs at real scale on a managed cluster. A mapping data flow isn't run on its own, though — it's operationalized inside a pipeline through a Data Flow activity, parameterizable and chainable exactly like any other activity from Chapters 3 and 4.
Next: Data Flow Debug Mode — actually watching your data transform, one single step at a time, against a live Spark cluster.
